title: Software Engineer
description:
iFIT ’s vision is to create the world's most holistic health and fitness platform, integrating all elements of health - physical fitness, mental health, nutrition and active recovery - into a seamless interactive experience. We develop proprietary software that learns and adjusts to the habits of each person as it delivers immersive content that guides them on their own individual fitness journey.

We are currently seeking an ambitious pace-setter to join our team as a Software Engineer remotely in the US.
iFIT is looking for a mid-to-senior level Software Engineer to design and build the backend services powering iFIT 's interactive fitness experiences. In this role, you will work on a service-oriented architecture in AWS, primarily using TypeScript and NestJS to create scalable microservices. Your contributions will directly impact millions of users worldwide, ensuring our platform remains reliable, performant, and primed for innovation. You will help drive the evolution of our APIs from REST to GraphQL, modernize legacy systems, and integrate with billing platforms such as Stripe, Apple, Google, and more. To facilitate collaboration, you must be available during core hours of 10 AM - 3 PM US Mountain Time, and will participate in a rotating on-call schedule approximately one week per rotation with the team.
ROLE COMMITMENTS

• Develop and maintain backend microservices in TypeScript and NestJS deployed via AWS ECS, ensuring services are well-designed, scalable, and aligned with our service-oriented architecture and best practices.

• Design, implement, and document robust RESTful APIs that are secure, efficient, and easy for client teams to use.

• Help migrate legacy serverless functions from AWS Lambda into containerized services on ECS, refactoring and re-architecting older systems for improved performance, maintainability, and consistency across the platform.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Work closely with front-end and mobile teams, product managers, and designers to deliver end-to-end features, clarify requirements, review designs, and ensure seamless integration across multiple services.

• Write clean, well-tested code and participate in peer code reviews, maintaining comprehensive unit and integration tests and continuously improving CI/CD pipelines.

• Take ownership of the reliability of the services you build, monitor performance, troubleshoot production issues, and participate in a rotating 24/7 on-call schedule to quickly address critical incidents and minimize downtime.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE
Education and Basic Qualifications

• 4+ years of professional software engineering experience building backend or full-stack applications in a cloud environment.

• Strong proficiency in TypeScript/JavaScript and Node.js with hands-on experience with backend frameworks - NestJS strongly preferred, or similar frameworks like Express/Koa with a willingness to learn NestJS.

• Solid knowledge of AWS services and architecture, with experience deploying and running containerized applications in AWS ECS, EKS, or similar, and familiarity with microservices, distributed systems, and event-driven architecture.

• Proven experience designing, building, and consuming RESTful APIs with a strong understanding of API security and performance considerations.

• Experience with relational and NoSQL databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB, as well as caching mechanisms such as Redis, with the ability to write efficient queries and optimize data access in a cloud environment.

• Comfortable with CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation, and knowledge of monitoring and logging tools such as CloudWatch and Datadog.

• Ability to jump into unfamiliar projects quickly and work across different services and tech stacks as needed.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills with a team-oriented mindset and a habit of knowledge sharing and proactive problem-solving.

title: Employee Engagement Programs Lead
description:
Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

About the Role
As our Engagement Program Lead, you'll own how Parachute comes together. You'll run the logistics and execution behind our employee programs including company offsite, our department and team gatherings, the moments where a remote-first company creates in-person collaboration to accelerate working relationships and shared learnings. You'll also keep our People & Culture programs running day to day, so they land on time and feel considered.
We're roughly 320 people and growing fast, which makes the scale of this work real: our annual company offsite now brings the whole company together, and department gatherings are multiplying faster than any one person can plan them. A big part of your first year is standing up Offsite-in-a-Box: a set of vetted vendors, templates, and budget tools that lets any department lead plan a great gathering without starting from scratch. This role sits at the center of two things we care about: making in-person time count, and making it easy for teams to create it themselves.
About the Team
People & Culture at Parachute is a small, senior team with a growing bench behind it. One side of the function owns how we organize, how we hire and pay, and how the function runs day to day. The other side owns what happens after someone joins: engagement and organizational insight, leadership and manager capability, and the moments that bring a remote-first company together.
You sit on the Employee Experience & Development side, reporting to the VP who owns the strategy and design of these programs.
The People & Culture team is growing with expanded programming and responsibilities, which means the systems you build become how we operate - and there is room to grow with the function.
Key Responsibilities
Company events and offsites

•
Company offsite: Own end-to-end logistics for our annual company offsite including venue and vendor sourcing, contracts, travel and rooming, run-of-show, on-site execution, and post-event reconciliation

•
Department gatherings: Support department leads planning their own offsites with sourcing, budget guidance, and a sounding board on agenda and logistics

•
Spend discipline: Track spend in real time against event budgets and reconcile with Finance after every event

•
Contract and vendor governance: Route vendor agreements above our signature threshold through Legal, and hold every vendor to W-9, certificate of insurance, and indemnification requirements before signature. No employee or confidential company data goes into event vendor tools.

•
Duty of care: Own traveler safety, emergency protocols, and accessibility requirements for company-sponsored travel and on-site events.

Offsite-in-a-Box

•
Build the toolkit: Own the intake form, planning templates, vetted vendor agreements, and budget calculator that let department leads run their own gatherings, maintained as a documented, current library you are the named steward of - structured so it can serve as context for our AI tooling, not just a shared drive folder

•
Onboard planners: Bring planners into the process and collect the post-event one-pager from each gathering

•
Iterate: Refine the toolkit each quarter based on what planners tell you is missing or getting in the way

•
Automate the coordination: Use AI tooling to take coordination time out of the process: intake triage, vendor comparison, first-draft budget reconciliation, and post-event synthesis. The t

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life - or even a third.

Our tech stack: Kubernetes, Terraform, Chef, Google Cloud Platform, Go, Kafka, Vespa, Redis, Vitess.

• Architect high-performance inference solutions, focusing on low-latency delivery and efficient GPU utilisation across our clusters.

• Define and drive reliability standards, including SLOs, error budgets, and sophisticated observability for model-serving systems.

• Mentor and grow senior engineers within the team, fostering a culture of technical excellence, pragmatism, and continuous learning.

• Identify and solve systemic bottlenecks in our deployment lifecycle by writing RFCs and sparring with colleagues on long-term architectural improvements.

• Oversee the integration of deployment workflows with automated experimentation patterns, such as A/B testing and shadow deployments.

• Communicate with stakeholders about architectural risks, planned changes, and strategic reliability trade-offs.

About you 

• Have a track record of leading technical problem-solving for complex, domain-level systems.

• Deeply experienced with Kubernetes, Linux internals, and high-scale networking.

Our mission is to build the next generation of high-performance and intelligent inference systems. We optimize not only how fast and efficiently models run, but also how quickly inference systems can adapt to new models, architectures, hardware, and workloads.

Our work spans the full inference stack-from distributed serving and runtime systems to GPU kernels and model-system co-design. description:
SENIOR MACHINE LEARNING ENGINEER (ALL GENDERS) - BABBEL LABS

ABOUT BABBEL LABS

Babbel Labs is building the future of language learning. We are an AI-first, independent company within the Babbel group, based in Berlin. Our teams bring AI, research and product together to ship experiences that set a new standard for how people learn.

THE ROLE

Babbel's learner-personalisation engine tracks what a learner has and hasn't mastered, and decides what they should practice next. We are actively pushing personalisation further; moving beyond describing a user and prescribing targeted practice, to adapting the learning journey ahead of them.

This is a hands-on senior individual-contributor role on that team. You will own real subsystems end to end and make decisions about how to improve the personalisation engine. That includes everything from research and benchmarking through production, monitoring and incidents that follow six months later.

HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT

- Work directly with the Principal Scientist to take designs from spec into production, then keep improving what you’ve built on your own judgement rather than waiting to be told what’s next.

- Help shape new features from the beginning - not just implementation of a spec handed to you.

- Take real ownership of core personalisation and mastery-tracking subsystems, operate independently, and make decisions confidently and competently.

- Design the evaluation that tells you whether a change is real: a rigorous offline benchmark against a real baseline, and the online experiment that confirms or kills it.

- Run what you build. Instrument it, notice when it's silently wrong rather than only when it errors, and fix it before it becomes an incident.

- Deliver with coding agents as a matter of course, and verify what they produce before you rely on it.

YOUR SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

- Strong, hands-on ML engineering that has shipped real models to production - recommendation, ranking, scoring, or trust-and-safety systems under real user load are the closest match. Research or competition experience is a plus.

- Experience with probabilistic modeling, latent-variable modeling and Bayesian inference, or the equivalent rigor from an adjacent domain.

- ML system evaluation: monitoring metrics you define, debugging output that doesn’t look right, and rolling out a change to a live scoring or ranking system without breaking it.

- Rigorous experimentation practice: benchmarking against a real baseline, running or reading A/B tests correctly, and the judgement to know when an offline improvement won't survive contact with production.

- TypeScript/Python as your primary languages, with enough command of our surrounding stack (AWS, Terraform, CI/CD) to ship and own your own service's delivery. This is not an infrastructure role, so depth there is not the bar.

- Coding agents are part of your daily workflow, and you check their output before you rely on it. You are neither dismissive of them nor careless with them.

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience with psychometric models, such as Item Response Theory.

- Graph ML experience - embeddings, graph neural networks, or relational modeling - at real scale.

- Public technical work: open-source contributions, writing, or competitive ML.

WAYS OF WORKING

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role on a small team that moves fast, agent-first, but with a disciplined delivery approach. It is remote and Berlin-friendly. The interview process is deliberately short: an initial screen, followed by one structured working session with the hiring manager.

title: 2014 Senior Embedded Software Engineer - Test OS
description:
Senior Embedded Software Engineer (SP1 - RVT):
¿Qué es?
Es un profesional especializado en el desarrollo, integración y adaptación de sistemas operativos embebidos (como Embedded Linux o RTOS) para ECUs (Unidades de Control Electrónico), con enfoque en la replicación y optimización de un Test OS en plataformas automotrices.
¿Cómo lo hace?
Analiza y porta el Test OS (usado para pruebas, diagnósticos y validación) de vehículos Gen2 a Gen1, adaptando su arquitectura, servicios y flujo de despliegue.
Desarrolla capas de abstracción de software para garantizar la compatibilidad entre el Test OS y el hardware de las ECUs.
Integra funcionalidades clave como diagnósticos (UDS, DoIP), flasheo de firmware, adquisición de datos (logging) y monitoreo de salud en tiempo real.
Automatiza pruebas (SIL, HIL y a nivel vehicular) para validar el comportamiento de las ECUs y los componentes conectados.
Depura problemas entre capas (software, hardware, comunicación) y colabora con equipos multidisciplinarios para cerrar brechas de plataforma.
¿Por qué es crucial?
Su trabajo asegura que los sistemas embebidos en vehículos Gen1 funcionen con la misma robustez y capacidad de prueba que los de Gen2, garantizando calidad, seguridad y cumplimiento de estándares automotrices (ej: ASPICE, MISRA C).
Requirements
Habilidades:
Lenguajes: C (avanzado +5 años), C++ (intermedio/avanzado 3-5+ años), Python (intermedio 2-5 años), Bash (intermedio 2-5 años).
Sistemas operativos embebidos: Embedded Linux (avanzado +5 años), RTOS (avanzado +5 años).
Protocolos de comunicación: CAN, CAN FD, UDS (avanzado +5 años), DoIP, Automotive Ethernet (intermedio 2-5 años).
Herramientas: Vector CANoe/CANalyzer/CANape (avanzado +5 años), GDB, JTAG (intermedio/avanzado 3-5+ años).
Pruebas automatizadas: GoogleTest, pytest (intermedio/avanzado 3-5+ años), SIL, HIL (avanzado +5 años).
CI/CD y control de versiones: Git (avanzado +5 años), Jenkins, GitLab CI (intermedio/avanzado 3-5+ años).
Firmware para ECUs: Integración, flasheo, diagnósticos (DIDs, DTCs) (avanzado +5 años).
Estándares: ASPICE, MISRA C (avanzado +5 años).
Visa (Obligatorio) - Viajaran a USA por el equipo de cliente
Actividades del puesto:
Análisis y adaptación del Test OS:
Analizar la arquitectura, servicios y flujo de despliegue del Test OS implementado en vehículos Gen2.
Portar el Test OS a las ECUs Gen1 de RVT, asegurando compatibilidad con el hardware existente.
Desarrollo de software embebido:
Desarrollar capas de abstracción de plataforma para facilitar la comunicación, control y monitoreo de las ECUs.
Implementar módulos de software para integración de diagnósticos, flasheo de firmware y adquisición de datos.
Integración de funcionalidades clave:
Integrar diagnósticos de ECU (DIDs, DTCs) usando protocolos como UDS y DoIP.

title: Senior Product Manager (AI CICD)
description:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. 

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

Senior Product Manager, AI CI/CD

The role, in a nutshell:

Chainguard secures the software supply chain, and we're standing up a new team to build a new product inside it.

Agents now write a large and growing share of the world's code, and they inherited a CI system designed for humans who push a few times a day. Write, push, wait in a queue, reinstall the same toolchain, scrape the logs, try again. Agents iterate far more often than people do, so they feel every minute of that, and the workarounds they've grown are worse than the thing they're working around. We don't think the fix is a faster version of the CI you already have. We think CI gets rebuilt for agents, and that's what we're doing.

The product isn't launched, so a job post is the wrong place for the details. What we can tell you now: the team is small, the hard technical pieces already run in production inside Chainguard, and you'd be driving the product direction. 

What you'll own:

• Strategy and roadmap. Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the product. Decide what we build first, what comes next, and what we're not going to do.

• 0→1 product work. Take this from a system that works for us to a product customers buy and use. Bring structure to problems that don't have any yet, make the tradeoff calls, and get things in front of users before they feel finished.

• How agents actually build software. Go deep on how developers and their agents write, test, review, and ship code today, including the parts nobody blogs about. Most of what's written about agentic development is aspirational. You'll work from what people really do.

• Design partners. Find the teams whose agent fleets are big enough to hurt, get the product into their hands early, and turn what they tell you into priorities.

• Developer experience. Adoption is the whole game here. Own how the product gets tried, configured, and lived with, so a team can move onto it without running a migration project.

• Launch. Positioning, naming, docs, the pricing model, and the story, with Product Marketing and the rest of Product. You're also the person who says when it's ready.

• Cross-functional leadership. Partner with Engineering, Experience, Product Marketing, and other Product leaders, and keep a small team pointed at the same thing while the space shifts underneath it.

What we're looking for:

• 5+ years of product management experience on developer-facing, infrastructure, security, or similarly technical products.

• You've built agent tools. Something agents use, or something people use to build with agents: a coding agent, an agent framework or harness, MCP servers, eval systems, or developer tooling meant to be driven by a model instead of a person. This is the requirement that matters most to us.

• You know CI from the inside. Builds, tests, caches, runners, artifacts, merge gates, and the specific reasons pipelines end up slow, flaky, and expensive. You should have opinions about why.

• You don't need to be a GitHub Actions expert. We're not building a better Actions, and years of workflow YAML isn't the experience we're hiring for. Knowing where it breaks is.

• Experience taking a technical product from an early idea through launch and iteration.

• Judgment about what to leave out. A new product dies from doing too much as easily as from doing too little.

title: Senior JavaScript Engineer (Full-stack, Retention)
description:

Relay Commerce is an e-commerce enablement platform offering scaling solutions across personalized messaging, social commerce, and customer retention, helping merchants navigate the rapidly evolving digital landscape with a comprehensive suite of tools. The Relay suite of solutions currently drives more than $1 billion in aggregate incremental gross merchandise volume for more than 35,000 merchants.

About the Role

This is a primarily back-end role (~70%) where you will design and evolve TypeScript services that power personalized replenishment, cross-sell, and subscription offers used by Shopify stores processing millions of transactions.

You will own features end-to-end, shaping the problem with a Senior Product Manager, proposing the architecture, implementing the solution with the support of AI, and monitoring and operating it in production. These systems need to be reliable, observable, maintainable, and performant.

You will effectively use AI agents such as Claude code and Codex to deliver at pace.

You will also contribute to our React-based front-ends (~30%) when delivering features as part of an experienced multi-functional team.

Relo, a Relay company, helps consumer goods and subscription brands unlock more than 30% additional revenue from their existing customers. The platform gets one-time buyers to order again, turns more customers into subscribers, and keeps them loyal. It does this through an engine that predicts when each customer is ready to reorder, making recurring revenue easy for scaling Shopify merchants.
Primary Responsibilities

• Work as part of a skilled, AI-native, multi-disciplined product engineering team to rapidly deliver modern software, to excellent quality standards, across high-volume subscription and billing systems.

• Design and deliver serverless TypeScript services on AWS Lambda, backed by MySQL and Prisma ORM.

• Contribute to efficient, modern React applications which rely on our APIs and integrate with the Shopify and Klaviyo ecosystems.

• Own features end-to-end, working with your team to make sure we ship solutions to real customer problems.

• Support our Customer Success team by joining our working hours escalation schedule, operating and maintaining the live production system.

• Participate in architectural discussions and technical decision making across Relo and the rest of Relay Commerce .

• Add agent context to codebases, run coding agents, build MCPs and AI product features to open our platform to LLMs such as Shopify’s Sidekick.

• Contribute improvements to processes, guidelines, and documentation in a fully-remote organisation.

Important Traits for Success

• You are comfortable taking loosely defined product ideas and turning them into concrete technical solutions.

• You effectively use AI agents such as Claude code or Codex to deliver working, reliable software at pace. You understand and can explain skills, MCP’s, RAG and other aspects of AI tooling. You know when to delegate to Claude and Codex, and when not to.

• You communicate clearly in writing. Design proposals, pull requests, and technical discussions should be concise and easy for other engineers to follow.

• You consider the operational impact of the systems you build. You think about reliability, observability, security, and performance before and during development.

• You are comfortable working across the stack when needed; front-end with React, back-end with REST APIs and CLI scripts, in the database, with infrastructure-as-code, or with cloud-native services.

• You take accountability

title: Technical Project Manager
description:
Ajaia is an AI implementation consultancy and product studio. We help organizations move from AI experimentation to measurable return on investment across four practices: AI Strategy and Advisory, Workforce Training and Enablement, Process Optimization, and Custom AI Development. Our work sits with executives and the people who do the actual work, and it is judged on whether something changed in production, not on whether a pilot looked good in a deck.
Position Overview
Ajaia is hiring a remote Technical Project Manager to run delivery on client AI builds from kickoff to a system that actually works in production. You will triage the pile of requests that lands on your desk this week, keep a mess of moving parts organized without dropping a thread, and know enough about the code to call out what will not hold up before a client ever sees it. You are not the person who decided what to build. You are the person who makes sure it gets built, on time, on scope, and honestly reported the whole way through.
This is a technical seat with a delivery mandate. You should be able to sit down and build a working automation yourself when that is faster than explaining to someone else what to build. We care far more about what you can build and run than how long you have held a title.
You will run delivery for US clients with a team based in New York. Client calls, standups, and escalations happen on US Eastern time, so this role is built around daily overlap with the US team, not asynchronous handoffs.
Compensation: Competitive, benchmarked to senior delivery roles in your market, plus a performance bonus tied to delivery outcomes. We will share a specific number for your location early in the process.
How we expect you to work
AI use is a core execution requirement at Ajaia, not optional tooling. You will use AI daily to draft status updates, stand up small automations, generate test data, and get a first pass on a code review, then apply your own judgment on top. Project managers at Ajaia write code: a script that cleans up a messy dataset, an automation that wires two systems together. You should be able to do that yourself, and comfortable saying when an AI-generated first draft is wrong.
Staying current on new tools is part of the job, and so is being straight with people: an engineer on a technical risk, a client on a date.
Remote works here when the writing is strong. Status, risks, and decisions get written down where the team and the client can read them, not held until the next call.
What you will do

• Build working automations and scripts yourself when that solves the problem faster than a meeting would.

• Read the code. Call out specifically what will break in production, not just whether the ticket is checked off.

• Keep a lot of moving parts straight at once: the backlog, the risk list, three overlapping deadlines, and whichever client is calling today.

• Triage ruthlessly. A pile of requests lands every week, and deciding what gets worked now and what waits is most of the job.

• Write to clients like a person. Plain, specific, and honest, especially when the news is not great.

• Run client calls and standups on US Eastern time and be reachable during the overlap window when something breaks.

• Own the delivery plan for your engagements end to end: sequencing, dependencies, and the date.

• Unblock technical decisions inside the team, then live with the consequence of the call you made.

• Escalate risks as soon as you see them, not after they have already cost the date.

• Define done for a deliverable before the engineer starts building it, not after they finish.

• Stay on the number after go-live long enough to know whether adoption is real or the dashboard is lying

Requirements

• Highly organized across many moving parts at once: a backlog, several risks, more than one client.

• Reads code and specs well enough to say what will break in production.

• Builds small automations and scripts to solve problems fast.

PATeam Software Consulting Ltd. delivers custom software product POS (ModusTech) and process-automation solutions for clients across the United States, the United Kingdom and Europe. We are strengthening our engineering leadership bench and are looking for a Technical Lead who can own the technical outcome of a React and .NET engagement end to end inclusive of writing code, guiding a team, and standing confidently in front of the client.
2. Role Purpose
The Technical Lead is accountable for the technical quality and on-time delivery of assigned React and .NET projects. This is a hands-on leadership role: roughly half the week is spent on design, code and review, and the remainder on guiding the team, planning sprints, managing dependencies and communicating with client stakeholders.
Success in this role means predictable delivery. Commitments made at sprint planning are met, risks are raised early rather than explained late, the codebase remains maintainable as the team scales, and the client regards you as the technical authority on the engagement.
3. Key Responsibilities
3.1 Technical leadership and hands-on engineering
Own the solution architecture for assigned projects across the front end (React) and back end (.NET), including component structure, API contracts, data models, authentication and integration patterns.
Contribute production code for the most complex or highest-risk parts of the solution, and set the standard the rest of the team follows.
Run code review as a quality gate - enforce coding standards, review pull requests within agreed turnaround times, and coach through review comments rather than simply rejecting work.
Make and document technical decisions with the trade-offs stated, so that choices can be revisited later without re-litigating them from scratch.
Own non-functional quality - performance, security, accessibility, scalability and maintainability are treated as delivery requirements, not afterthoughts.
Manage technical debt deliberately by maintaining a visible register and negotiating remediation into the sprint plan.
3.2 Agile delivery and schedule control
Lead sprint planning, estimation and backlog refinement with the Product Owner and Project Manager, and hold the team to realistic, defensible commitments.

title: Cyber Enablement Lead, Government
description:
About the Team

The Adoption, Innovation, and Transformation team within OpenAI for Government helps government organizations turn OpenAI products into durable capabilities and measurable mission impact.

We work alongside public servants to move from initial exploration to confident, responsible, organization-wide use of AI. Our work combines hands-on enablement, adoption strategy, deployment support, community, content, and practical transformation tailored to government missions and operating environments.

By translating the potential of OpenAI’s technology into better individual workflows, stronger teams, and improved public services, we help government customers deepen adoption, build lasting organizational capability, and spend more time on mission.

About the Role

We are seeking a Cyber Enablement Lead to join our Training and Enablement team and help government cyber professionals turn Daybreak’s capabilities into stronger defenses and measurable mission outcomes. This is a priority hire, and we are looking for someone who can join as soon as possible.

You will own Daybreak’s product enablement strategy and personally design, execute, and lead the training that brings it to life. Your work will span audience research, curriculum design, script writing, recorded demonstrations and courses, hands-on workshops, executive briefings, and our cyber councils.

You will work with Authorizing Officials (AOs), CISOs, cyber operators, developers, and senior executives, adapting the depth and format to each audience. Practitioners need practical proficiency; executives need a strategic understanding of our cyber products, their value, and their implications for mission and risk. Success means demonstrated capability, sustained adoption, and better cyber outcomes.

This role is based in Washington, D.C. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Travel and regular work from government customer sites are required.

In this role, you will:

- Own the end-to-end Daybreak enablement strategy: identify audience needs, define learning objectives, build curricula, deliver programs, and measure operational impact.

- Personally lead technical training, live demonstrations, workshops, and conversations with AOs, CISOs, cyber operators, and developers.

- Write scripts and record product demos and training. Create interactive labs, digital courses, videos, facilitator materials, and practical playbooks that make complex capabilities accessible and immediately useful.

- Host and facilitate our cyber councils, creating engaging discussions, drawing out questions, and helping participants learn from one another.

- Build bespoke, hands-on engagements for small specialist teams and scalable learning programs that reach thousands of practitioners.

- Connect Daybreak’s capabilities, applications, and deployment requirements to real government cyber workflows across the cybersecurity lifecycle.

- Partner closely with product, security, deployment, and customer teams to keep enablement technically accurate, responsive to feedback, and current as products and requirements evolve.

- Assess demonstrated proficiency, track adoption and sustained use, and improve programs based on learning evidence and measurable cyber and mission outcomes.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Bring deep knowledge of the cybersecurity lifecycle, including threat modeling, vulnerability discovery and validation, prioritization, remediation, detection, incident response, and recovery.

- Have comprehensive fluency in Daybreak’s capabilities, applications, and deployment requirements, and can translate that knowledge into useful government cyber training.

- Have a proven record of personally building and delivering cybersecurity product enablement, from specialist-team engagements to scaled programs for thousands of practitioners.

title: Senior Data Scientist
company: Atria Physician Practice New York PC
description:
The Atria Health Institute is a membership-based primary and specialty health care practice with a focus on prevention and longevity. We bring together a multidisciplinary team of renowned physicians to provide proactive, preventive, and precision-based care for Atria members and their families. All care, including primary care, advanced screening and diagnostics, urgent care, specialty care, 24/7 home visits, and imaging is included in members’ annual fee.
Our mission is to make healthspan and lifespan equal for all by translating science into medicine in real-time, all while bringing humanity back into health care. Delivering such robust, personalized, and preventive health care is complex and requires a team-wide dedication to excellence.
We have state-of-the-art facilities with imaging and diagnostics on-site in New York City, Palm Beach, and Los Angeles, with home services hubs in Miami, Greenwich/Westchester, and the Hamptons in summer. Additional locations are forthcoming in the Bay Area, Miami, and in downtown Manhattan. At each of our Institutes, we deliver personalized preventive medicine grounded in up-to-the-minute science - all in serene environments designed for trust and comfort.
Role Overview
As a Senior Data Scientist at Atria, you will generate the medical insights and forecasts that shape how our clinicians care for members and how Atria runs as a practice. You'll work with one of the most distinctive longitudinal datasets in medicine: deep per-member baselines (whole-genome sequencing, advanced imaging, comprehensive labs, movement analysis, lifestyle inputs) revisited on cadence over years and linked across full family lineages, alongside the operational data of how a multi-disciplinary care team actually delivers that care. Your work spans both sides of that equation: surfacing clinically meaningful patterns clinicians can act on, and building the analyses, forecasts, and operational models that help Atria deliver better care more efficiently.
What you'll do
• Generate medical insights from Atria's longitudinal clinical data: surface early signals of disease, characterize how members respond to interventions, and identify population-level trends clinicians can act on.
• Build forecasting models on clinical and operational signals: disease progression, biomarker trajectories, member engagement, demand and capacity planning, and other time-series problems.
• Lead or contribute to operational analytics: visit patterns, throughput and scheduling, panel composition, vendor performance, member journeys, and the quiet efficiency questions that compound over a year. • Design and execute studies in partnership with clinicians: clear questions, well-controlled comparisons, honest error analysis, and writeups that hold up to clinical scrutiny.
• Design and analyze experiments (A/B tests, staged rollouts, quasi-experiments) with appropriate attention to power, multiple comparisons, and the difference between "statistically significant" and "actually mattered".
• Author and maintain curated views and dbt models in our Snowflake gold layer, documented well enough that clinicians and operational staff can use them confidently without a Slack DM to you every Tuesday.
• Build dashboards and analytical tools in Omni Analytics that clinicians and operational leaders actually use to make decisions.
• Partner with the AI Scientists and AI Engineers on the boundary where analytical work meets model training and production systems: contributing ground truth, evaluation datasets, and the clinical framing that keeps their models pointed at the right problem.
• Translate clinical and operational questions into well-formed analytical problems, and translate results back into clear recommendations. The translation in both directions is most of the job.

The Data Center Engineering team designs training and inference compute clusters from first principles, pushing thermal, electrical, and optical systems to the limit of physics. We operate as a highly cross-disciplinary team of mechanical, electrical, optical, and software engineers, all working to maximize the efficiency, reliability, and deployment speed of terrestrial computing to serve rapidly scaling demand.

This team owns compute architecture, datacenter network design, rack builds, connectivity, in-house design of our own computers, and the manufacturing line that builds that compute.
